title: Your first instruction: print
idea: print(...) tells the computer to show something on the screen. First real code.

exercises.prompt: In Python, which instruction shows something on the screen?
exercises.explanation: print(...) is Python's instruction for showing output. It's the one you'll use most at first.

exercises.prompt:
What does this show on the screen?

print("Hello")
exercises.explanation: print shows what's inside the ( ). The quotes just mark the text — they aren't shown.

exercises.prompt: The quotes " " are shown on the screen along with the text.
exercises.explanation: Quotes mark where the text starts and ends. print("Hi") shows Hi, not "Hi".

exercises.prompt: Build an instruction that shows the word Dailo.
exercises.explanation: print, then ( , then your text in quotes, then ). This shows: Dailo

exercises.prompt:
Complete the instruction so it shows the word Hi:

print(____)
exercises.explanation: Text goes in quotes inside the brackets. Single or double quotes both work.

exercises.prompt: Which one correctly shows the word Cat?
exercises.explanation: Lowercase print, brackets, and quotes around the text. The others are each missing one piece — we'll meet those mistakes soon.

exercises.prompt: Build an instruction that shows: Good morning
exercises.explanation: The whole phrase, spaces and all, goes inside one pair of quotes.

exercises.prompt: print("123") will show 123 on the screen.
exercises.explanation: Anything inside the quotes is shown exactly — even if it looks like a number.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

print("I can code")
exercises.explanation: The text inside the quotes, shown exactly: I can code.

exercises.prompt: Write a full instruction that shows the word Yes.
exercises.explanation: print, brackets, quotes: print("Yes"). You just wrote real code!
